mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate applied to equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds continuously across the entire range of observed FEDFUNDS levels.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals a weakening labor market that reduces corporate profit growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and corporate earnings growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The effect is multiplicative: the return impact is stronger when both series rise together than when either rises alone.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20d returns on PAYEMS and RSAFS changes, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 3.5% and rising), high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signals persistent inflationary pressures that lead to aggressive rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 3.5% with rising rates, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL in this regime is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with stronger economic growth and higher corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This relationship holds continuously across the entire range of observed UNRATE levels.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for UNRATE in predicting 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between UNRATE and 60-day returns is not positive in the majority of 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1.0% over the past three months indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls > 1.0% (3mo), or the Rank IC for INDPRO in this condition is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The effect is multiplicative: the return impact is stronger when both series rise together than when either rises alone.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 5d returns on HOUST and RSAFS changes, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market recovery (HOUST rising above 1200.0 units for two consecutive months), strong housing activity signals a rebound in consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in less than 50% of instances when HOUST > 1200.0 and rising (2mo), or the Rank IC for HOUST in this regime is below 0.02.
